F1.context: A physics experiment: a ball is dropped onto a plank and bounces. Maintain structural integrity and object consistency throughout: no changing shapes, no blending, and no flashing background.

actions.description: The robot gripper holds the black ball still high above the plank, then its fingers open.

The ball drops straight down at real speed under gravity, falling about 40 cm and hitting the plank in about 0.3 seconds, then bounces several quick times with rapidly diminishing heights and comes to rest on the plank.
The ball lies motionless on the plank; the robot arm stays still. Nothing else moves.

segments.description: The ball is held still in the gripper above the plank; the gripper opens.

Real-time free fall: the ball accelerates downward under gravity, hits the plank within about a third of a second, rebounds to about a third of its drop height, then bounces lower and faster until it settles.
segments.key_changes: Fast fall, impact, quick diminishing bounces

segments.description: The ball rests on the plank without moving.

F1.temporal_caption: The black ball is held still in the robot gripper high above the wooden plank. At about one second, the gripper opens and the ball drops straight down at real speed under gravity, falling about 40 centimeters and striking the plank roughly 0.3 seconds after release. It rebounds to about 14 centimeters, then bounces several more times, each bounce lower and quicker, and settles on the plank before the two-second mark. For the rest of the video the ball lies motionless on the plank and nothing else moves.
